transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-29 15:10 (EST) | Duration 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Taylor Morgan (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Kai Nguyen (Redwood SE), Marta Diaz (CISO - Cobalt), Evan Brooks (Security Eng - Cobalt), Samantha Lee (Infra Lead - Cobalt), Liam O'Neill (Product)

[00:00:00] Taylor Morgan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we know you all had the pen test results come in last week, so today's agenda is to run through the findings, figure out triage/prioritization, and sync on patch cadence and any infra blockers for private or VPC deployment options.
[00:00:18] Marta Diaz: thanks Taylor, appreciate it. we want to be pragmatic—Cobalt's production is PCI scoped in a few EU regions so data residency and key management are pretty important for us.
[00:00:28] Jordan Patel: got it. quick intro from my side, I'm Jordan, SE focused on infra and KMS/HSM integrations; Kai here will also chime on runtime and patch impacts.
[00:00:37] Kai Nguyen: hi everyone.
[00:00:40] Evan Brooks: quick note—pen test vendor flagged 12 findings: 2 critical, 4 high, rest medium/low. we circulated the full report but there are a couple of ones we want to talk about in detail.
[00:00:52] Taylor Morgan: ok, can you recap the criticals? we have limited notes from the vendor but did want to make sure we cover mitigations and timelines.
[00:01:00] Evan Brooks: first critical was a deserialization flaw in a third-party ingestion service—something like unsanitized protobuf handling, vendor called it CVE-2025-1234 in their write-up, exploiting remote code possible if unauthenticated ingest endpoint reached. second critical was a misconfiguration that exposed debug endpoints in staging that are routable from the customer VPC when peering was set.
[00:01:27] Jordan Patel: ok, that protobuf-type CVE, that looks like a transitive dependency in the ingestion pipeline. typical fix is bumping the dependency and applying a sanitizer layer; will require a build-and-test cycle. for the debug endpoint, that sounds like a network ACL/ingress rule—should be a low-effort config change but we need to confirm the change window.
[00:01:50] Marta Diaz: yep, we see the PRs showing fixes but want the timeline—our compliance team requires remediation for criticals within 7 days and evidence for SOC 2 scope.
[00:01:59] Taylor Morgan: understood. Jordan, can you speak to our emergency patch SLA and whether we can push a hotfix out-of-band?
[00:02:07] Jordan Patel: Redwood supports emergency patching; for Dedicated or Private deployments we can push a hotfix in an emergency change with a rollback snapshot. Hosted tenants are handled via our normal deploy pipeline but we do have an expedited path for critical CVEs—typical lead time 24-72 hours depending on testing.
[00:02:27] Samantha Lee: how does rollback/restore work if a hotfix causes regression? we have strict change control.
[00:02:33] Kai Nguyen: we create immutable snapshots of the serving nodes and KV cache backups; rollback is a controlled rollback of the serving fleet and cache warmup. for high-throughput configs there is a short warmup period but we've done this in prod with 15–30 minute impact windows historically.
[00:02:51] Liam O'Neill: okay just to be clear—Cobalt requires evidence of testing and a post-mortem for any out-of-band changes.
[00:02:57] Taylor Morgan: that makes sense. we'll provide test artifacts and the smoke-test playbook. Jordan, you mentioned KMS—Marta, what are your requirements around key custody?
[00:03:07] Marta Diaz: we need customer-managed keys for EU-resident data and key rotation policies that meet our policy—90 day rotation, HSM backed preferred, and full audit logs showing key usage. also SSO integration is mandatory—SAML with Okta currently.
[00:03:22] Jordan Patel: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed KMS integrations via Cloud KMS/HSM; we can do envelope encryption so customer keys never leave their KMS. Key rotation can be automated. audit logs for key ops are available and we can ship KMS usage logs as part of the SOC 2 evidence bundle.
[00:03:38] Evan Brooks: on audit logs, retention requirements: we need 13 months for most auth/audit events and the ability to export to our SIEM (we use Splunk). can you stream logs?
[00:03:49] Kai Nguyen: yes, we have log forwarding to S3/Cloud Storage and direct streaming to SIEMs via a connector; retention policies can be configured per-tenant when on Dedicated/Private. in hosted we retain 90 days by default but enterprise plans can extend retention.
[00:04:02] Marta Diaz: so we probably need Private or Dedicated to hit our retention + KMS requirements.
[00:04:08] Taylor Morgan: that's a common pattern. we should map which controls require Private vs which are achievable on Hosted with add-ons. we'll follow up with a short doc.
[00:04:17] [00:04:20] Jordan Patel: back to vuln management—what is your internal triage SLA? how fast do you typically patch high/critical?
[00:04:26] Evan Brooks: we aim at 7 days for critical, 30 days for high, but we still have backlog and we need Redwood's help on showing remediation evidence quickly so auditors close the loop.
[00:04:36] Taylor Morgan: understood. our process for a critical CVE: confirm fix, run CI and an augmented test harness against a staging snapshot, deploy via emergency pipeline, and provide logs and repro + remediation PRs to you. that matches your 7-day goal depending on scheduling.
[00:04:50] Samantha Lee: what's the SAST/DAST coverage? we want to know how much of your supply chain you scan—containers, base images, language deps.
[00:04:59] Jordan Patel: we run SAST on PRs (covering server code and infra-as-code templates), DAST against staging environments weekly, and SBOM generation on every release. dependencies are scanned with a dependency scanner and critical transitive deps are flagged; we also integrate Dependabot style PRs for common languages.
[00:05:16] Marta Diaz: ok good. in the vendor report there were a couple of medium issues around image hardening and missing image signing. is image signing on the roadmap?
[00:05:25] Kai Nguyen: image signing is available for Private/Dedicated customers; for Hosted it's in beta but we can enable image signature verification for your account if you need it.
[00:05:33] Evan Brooks: another point: the vendor called out RBAC gaps—some service accounts had elevated privileges to K8s API. we need a short-term mitigation plan.
[00:05:43] Jordan Patel: short-term we can rotate service account tokens and lock down roles; medium-term we push least-privilege IAM roles and OPA/Gatekeeper policies. we can provide an RBAC audit report and recommended role mappings.
[00:05:55] [00:06:00] Taylor Morgan: good. can we get an expected ETA for the RBAC audit report?
[00:06:04] Jordan Patel: I can turn a draft report around in 3 business days and include remediation PRs.
[00:06:10] Marta Diaz: fine. about SSO—we plan to use Okta SAML for console and SSO for API—do you enforce SCIM provisioning?
[00:06:20] Kai Nguyen: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC ties to SCIM groups. we can also do SCIM-based de-provisioning to satisfy your offboarding policy.
[00:06:31] Marta Diaz: perfect.
[00:06:33] [00:06:40] Evan Brooks: some of the remediation steps in the vendor's spreadsheet reference parameter changes in the runtime that could affect latency—are those safe to change?
[00:06:48] Jordan Patel: depends which parameters—some buffer tuning and logging level changes are safe; others, like very aggressive GC or quantization toggles, need careful load testing. we'll annotate each recommended change with expected perf impact.
[00:07:03] Taylor Morgan: side note: you asked about data residency—we have hosted regions in EU-west and can do Private deployments on your VPC. Key point: for EU-resident workloads with customer-managed keys and 13+ months of audit retention, Dedicated or Private is the right fit.
[00:07:21] Marta Diaz: that's helpful. one more compliance ask—the auditor will need to see our change window and emergency change policy with all post-change evidence. can Redwood commit to providing that?
[00:07:32] Taylor Morgan: yes, we'll provide an emergency change runbook, logs, and rollback evidence. we'll also share our SOC 2 artifact bundle and ISO cert link.
[00:07:42] [00:07:55] Samantha Lee: practical question—what is the normal monthly patch cadence and how disruptive is it?
[00:07:59] Kai Nguyen: our normal cadence is weekly security deploys to staging and monthly production maintenance windows; customers can opt-in to more frequent windows. typical maintenance windows are low-impact—rolling restarts of workers, with <5% transient capacity impact if autoscaling is configured.
[00:08:17] Evan Brooks: and for emergency hotfixes do you require a maintenance window?
[00:08:21] Jordan Patel: for emergency patches we do an expedited window; for Dedicated/Private we align with your on-call and change control and can execute outside normal windows with your approval.
[00:08:32] Marta Diaz: ok. going back to the pen test, can you talk through the re-test flow? vendor wants evidence that fixes were verified by the same tooling or a follow-up verification.
[00:08:41] Taylor Morgan: we can do two options: 1) Redwood runs an internal smoke re-test and provides the results and artifacts to you; 2) coordinate a vendor re-test with the pen test company. typically for critical findings we recommend the vendor re-test; Redwood will run a parallel internal verification to speed things up.
[00:08:58] Evan Brooks: vendor re-test will be their call, but having Redwood's internal verification speeds up closure.
[00:09:03] [00:09:15] Jordan Patel: note on supply chain—we'll produce SBOMs for the service and container images and include transitive dependencies; that should help you demonstrate CVE closure.
[00:09:26] Marta Diaz: SBOMs plus patch PR links should satisfy auditors.
[00:09:30] Taylor Morgan: quick recap of decisions so far: Redwood to share redacted pen test report (Taylor), Jordan will produce RBAC audit and remediation PRs, Cobalt to confirm patch windows and emergency SLA, and both teams to aim for an expedited hotfix path for the two critical items within 7 days. anything missing?
[00:09:49] Evan Brooks: we also need the exact log forwarding config for Splunk ingestion—endpoint, auth, and sample event format.
[00:09:57] Kai Nguyen: will include connector docs and sample events in the follow-up.
[00:10:02] Samantha Lee: and please include the KMS audit log format and rotation evidence.
[00:10:06] Jordan Patel: yes.
[00:10:10] [00:10:25] Taylor Morgan: great. any other open risks?
[00:10:28] Marta Diaz: the only other thing is the vendor noted a couple of discovery issues where internal test credentials were left in a repo snapshot. that seems like a secure-SDLC control gap.
[00:10:39] Jordan Patel: for SDLC gaps we recommend pre-commit hooks, secret scanning, SAST gating, and pull-request rules. we can share our PR template and scanning config as examples.
[00:10:50] Evan Brooks: do you run a bug bounty program or external attack surface monitoring?
[00:10:55] Kai Nguyen: we run external attack surface monitoring and have a coordinated disclosure program; a formal bug bounty is in scope for enterprise customers on a case-by-case basis.
[00:11:05] [00:11:20] Taylor Morgan: ok let's be explicit on timelines: Jordan you said RBAC audit in 3 business days, Taylor to send redacted pen test by EOD 12/2, Cobalt to confirm monthly vs weekly patch windows by 12/05. Jordan to put tentative re-test week of 12/15 for critical items. is that all?
[00:11:35] Marta Diaz: yes.
[00:11:36] [00:11:45] Liam O'Neill: on the commercial side, will enabling Private change pricing materially? we need an estimate for budgeting.
[00:11:52] Taylor Morgan: Dedicated/Private do change pricing; I'll share a pricing snapshot and a rough TCO delta in the follow-up. no binding quote in this call.
[00:11:59] [00:12:10] Evan Brooks: last question—do you provide immutable audit logs or tamper-evident logs?
[00:12:16] Kai Nguyen: yes, we can configure append-only logs with integrity checks and ship to your customer-managed S3 with object lock for immutability if required.
[00:12:25] Marta Diaz: that's ideal.
[00:12:28] [00:12:40] Taylor Morgan: ok wrapping up—thanks everyone. we'll send the redacted pen test report, a remediation spreadsheet, RBAC audit, and connectors docs. Jordan will coordinate the re-test once we have fixes.
[00:12:52] Marta Diaz: thanks, appreciate the quick turn.
[00:12:55] Evan Brooks: thanks all.
[00:13:00] Taylor Morgan: meeting over. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the re-test and send the artifact links.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had occasional misheard technical names (protobuf/OPa vs OPA), and speaker turns were cleaned lightly but some overlaps remain.
notes: Transcription includes natural speech artifacts and occasional mis-recognitions (e.g., OPA/OPa, CVE identifiers are vendor-provided). Follow-up artifacts: redacted pen test report, remediation spreadsheet, RBAC audit, SOC2 evidence bundle, KMS audit logs sample, Splunk connector config.
